papers.title_zh: NLST事后分析：筛查适格当前吸烟者中，近期戒烟与死亡率的关联幅度大于LDCT筛查
papers.title_en: Low-dose CT Screening and Smoking Cessation: Separate and Joint Associations with Mortality among Ever-Smokers Eligible for Lung Cancer Screening.
papers.authors: Wang H, Frick C, Sha S, Edelmann D, Bhardwaj M, Brenner H
papers.affiliation_highlight: Cancer Prevention Graduate School, German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), Heidelberg, Germany; Heidelberg Medical Faculty…
papers.results: 31,560人中7,197人（22.8%）全因死亡，中位随访12.3年；30,915人纳入病因特异性分析，1,783人（5.8%）肺癌死亡。筛查适格当前吸烟者中，LDCT较CXR肺癌死亡风险降低12%（HR 0.88；95%CI 0.79-0.97），全因死亡无显著降低（HR 0.98；95%CI 0.93-1.03）。CXR组中，近期戒烟者较持续吸烟者肺癌死亡与全因死亡均显著更低（HR分别为0.62，95%CI 0.51-0.76；0.68，95%CI 0.62-0.75）；LDCT组近期戒烟者观察到相似幅度的降低（摘要未给出该组具体数值）。
papers.authors_conclusion: 对于筛查适格的当前吸烟者，近期戒烟所伴随的肺癌死亡和全因死亡降幅显著大于LDCT筛查所关联的降幅；这些发现强调了将有效戒烟干预整合进肺癌筛查项目的重要性。
papers.ai_note: 标题声称'分开与联合关联'，但摘要仅报告筛查与戒烟各自的关联，未提供任何联合暴露或交互作用的数值，联合分析结果信息不足。将随机化的LDCT vs CXR比较与观察性的戒烟 vs 持续吸烟比较的HR幅度直接对比，两类效应量并非等价可比，且戒烟为非随机暴露，存在健康戒烟者偏倚（如疾病促使戒烟的反向因果）。'近期戒烟'以入组前2年内戒烟作为筛查启动时戒烟的代理，属代理指标。LDCT组戒烟的具体数值在摘要中缺失，'相似降低'无数据支撑。LDCT全因死亡未达统计学显著。

pico.p: NLST中符合肺癌筛查条件的持续吸烟者与近期戒烟者共31,560人（其中30,915人纳入病因特异性分析），中位随访12.3年
pico.ic: 干预/暴露1：LDCT筛查 vs 胸部X线（CXR）筛查（随机分配）；干预/暴露2：入组前2年内戒烟（近期戒烟）vs 持续吸烟（观察性比较）

papers.reason: 为肺癌筛查项目是否必须配套戒烟干预提供真实世界证据权重，影响筛查项目设计与资源配置中戒烟干预的优先级判断；同时提示用非等价比较支撑强结论的方法学风险，可作为筛查相关研究的批判性阅读素材。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Smoking cessation intervention is increasingly recognized as a core component of high-quality lung cancer screening (LCS). However, real-world evidence that compares the health effects of low-dose CT (LDCT) screening, smoking cessation, and their combination among screening-eligible current smokers remains limited. METHODS: We conducted a post-hoc analysis of data of the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST), defining recent quitting as smoking cessation within 2 years before enrolment as a proxy for cessation occurring close to screening initiation. Cox proportional hazards models were used to quantify associations of screening allocation and smoking cessation with LC-specific and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Among 31,560 continuous smokers and recent quitters included in the analysis, 7,197 (22.8%) died from any cause during a median follow-up of 12.3 years. Of 30,915 participants included in cause-specific analyses, 1,783 (5.8%) died from LC. Among current smokers eligible for LCS, LDCT was associated with 12% lower LC mortality than chest radiography (CXR) (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.79-0.97), but no significant reduction of all-cause mortality (HR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.93-1.03). In the CXR arm, recent quitting was associated with substantially lower LC and all-cause mortality than continued smoking (HRs, 0.62 and 0.68; 95% CIs, 0.51-0.76 and 0.62-0.75, respectively), with similar reductions observed among recent quitters in the LDCT arm. CONCLUSIONS: For screening-eligible current smokers, recent quitting was associated with substantially larger reductions in LC and all-cause mortality than those associated with LDCT screening. These findings reinforce the importance of integrating effective smoking cessation interventions into LCS programs.

papers.authors: Warkentin MT, Ruan Y, Harsanyi H, Mullin ML, Brenner DR, Tremblay A, O'Sullivan DE
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Oncology, Cumming School of Medicine, University of Calgary, Calgary, Canada.
papers.results: 癌症幸存者总体发生后续原发性肺癌（SIR）=1.37，95%CI 1.32–1.42；晚期（III/IV期）SPLC风险升高，且FPC诊断5年后晚期SPLC风险升高幅度最大；21个FPC部位中约13个SPLC风险显著升高，吸烟相关FPC部位风险最高；头颈癌、膀胱癌幸存者6年SPLC绝对风险分别为2.7%和2.6%；5个FPC部位的SIR高于肺癌筛查试验对照组；SPLC风险随年龄、性别、社会经济状况、合并症、FPC分期与治疗而异

papers.ai_note: 信息不足/疑点：①观察性登记研究，幸存者接受影像随访更多，SIR升高可能部分源于监测偏倚（surveillance bias），摘要未说明是否校正；②将6年绝对风险2.7%/2.6%与筛查入组阈值直接比较、以及5个部位SIR与筛查试验对照组比较，均为跨研究间接对比，非同一人群验证；③21个部位多重比较未见校正说明；④Fine-Gray模型的具体协变量、亚分布HR及CI未在摘要给出；⑤研究仅评估发病风险，未评估筛查这些幸存者能否降低死亡率，筛查获益无证据支持。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: An increasing number of people are living with and beyond a cancer diagnosis. We aim to characterize the risk of developing a subsequent primary lung cancer (SPLC) among survivors of non-lung first primary cancers (FPC). METHODS: All adults diagnosed with cancer in Alberta between 2000 and 2021 who survived 6+ months were included. We estimated incidence rate differences and standardized incidence ratios (SIR) for SPLC compared to the cancer-free population and high-risk individuals included in a lung cancer screening trial. Multivariable Fine-Gray models were used to identify risk factors within cancer survivorship groups. RESULTS: Cancer survivors (n = 180,325) have a higher risk of developing SPLC compared to those without a personal cancer history overall (SIR = 1.37, 95% Confidence Interval: 1.32-1.42) and at later stages (III/IV). The increase in late-stage SPLC risk was highest beyond 5 years from FPC diagnosis. About 13 out of 21 FPC sites have significant increases in SPLC risk and smoking-related FPC sites carried the highest risks. For survivors of head and neck or bladder cancers, the 6-year absolute risks of developing SPLC were 2.7% and 2.6%, respectively, which is higher than the thresholds commonly used for lung screening program eligibility. Five FPC sites had SIRs higher than the control arm of a lung cancer screening trial. Site-specific SPLC risk varied by age, sex, socioeconomic status, comorbidities, stage of FPC, and treatments. CONCLUSION: Cancer survivors carry significant risks of developing SPLC yet many survivors may not be considered for long term surveillance or screening for early lung cancer detection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Mediastinal paragangliomas are rare neuroendocrine tumors, leading to potentially invasive clinical investigation and inadequate staging. Functional secretory activity, high germline mutation rates, multifocal disease burden, and proximity to the great vessels demand a multidisciplinary approach. We describe our longitudinal multidisciplinary experience building a center of excellence model. METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of 19 patients with mediastinal paraganglioma managed at a quaternary referral center, capturing demographics, imaging, preoperative testing, operative details, and perioperative outcomes. RESULTS: There were 14 (73.7%) females with a median age of 46.3 years (IQR 38.5-57.6 years). Sixteen (84%) of 19 patients were referred from outside centers; 9 (47.3%) underwent biopsy before referral, with three (15.8%) experiencing catecholamine crisis, pneumothorax, or hemorrhage. Nine (47.4%) tumors were adjacent to the aorta, and seven (42.1%) adjacent to the pulmonary artery, with vascular involvement in 17(89.5%) of the 19 patients. Thirteen (68%) were functional and five (26.3%) had multifocal disease. Succinate dehydrogenase mutations were found in 63.6% of patients tested. Cardiopulmonary bypass was required in 63.2%, with zero 30-day mortality. Postoperative complications occurred in 47.4%, predominantly atrial arrhythmia. Median hospital stay was four days. Four patients developed local recurrence at a median recurrence-free survival of 16.9 months, all with positive margins or multifocal disease. CONCLUSIONS: Mediastinal paragangliomas can be safely resected within a multidisciplinary center of excellence. Early recognition, avoidance of uninformed biopsy, functional staging, preoperative alpha blockade, and tumor profiling and genetic evaluation with genetic counseling are essential components.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate a multidimensional radiomics signature utilizing fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT) and machine learning to accurately differentiate peripheral pulmonary tuberculosis from primary peripheral lung cancer. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 346 patients (144 peripheral pulmonary tuberculosis, 202 lung cancer). Radiomic features were extracted from pretreatment PET/CT scans. Patients were randomly split 7:3 into training (n = 242) and internal validation (n = 104) sets. Due to the short 3-year enrollment period with stable protocols, random splitting was the primary validation method. A temporal split (first 70% vs. most recent 30%) was also performed as a sensitivity analysis to assess temporal robustness. Three classifiers (random forest, support vector machine, gradient boosting machine) were compared. The optimal model was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: The final model incorporated six key predictors: age, maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), metabolic heterogeneity index (CV%), PET skewness, PET gray-level co-occurrence matrix energy (PET-GLCM Energy), and shape sphericity. All were identified as independent predictors via multivariate logistic regression (all P < 0.05). The random forest model demonstrated superior and stable performance, achieving an AUC of 0.861 (95% CI: 0.805-0.917) in training and 0.833 (95% CI: 0.732-0.934) in internal validation set. Calibration curves indicated good agreement between predictions and observations. Furthermore, decision curve analysis confirmed the model's clinical net benefit across a wide threshold probability range. CONCLUSION: A machine learning model based on multidimensional ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT radiomics features was developed and internally validated. This model demonstrates robust discriminatory efficacy, good calibration, and clinical utility for differentiating peripheral pulmonary tuberculosis from lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Smoking prevalence varies greatly by sex across Europe. In Spain, while smoking prevalence has decreased in men, it has risen in women in the past decades and is now amongst the highest in Europe. However, there has been limited research into how changes in smoking prevalence impact long-term lung cancer incidence. This study analyses sex and birth-cohort specific smoking patterns in Spain and their impact on future lung cancer incidence. METHODS: We used the MIcrosimulation SCreening Analysis (MISCAN)-Lung to evaluate and project smoking behaviour patterns and lung cancer incidence in Spain by sex and birth-cohort, using cancer registry data and nationally representative surveys from years 1987-2020. FINDINGS: By 2035, current smoking prevalence in women born between 1955-1969 is expected to be higher than men (19.1 % current smoking prevalence for women compared to 14.1 % in men for the 1965-1969 birth-cohort). In men, lung cancer incidence per 100,000 person-years between 2015 and 2035 for those aged 55-64 and 65-79 is expected to decrease by 57.6 % (from 193.3 to 82.0 per 100,000) and 13.0 % (from 329.8 to 287.0 per 100,000), respectively. While a similar decline in incidence is projected for women aged 55-64 (from 74.5 to 29.8 per 100,000; 60.0 % decrease), incidence in ages 65-79 will increase by 171.6 % (from 48.6 to 132.0 per 100,000). INTERPRETATION: Lung cancer incidence in women aged 65-79 in Spain is expected to increase considerably in the next decade. Given the variation in smoking prevalence by sex across Europe, the evaluation of sex differentiated prevention and early detection strategies for lung cancer are pivotal.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2/ERBB2) mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is associated with poor prognosis and limited treatment options. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used electronic health records from US academic and community cancer centers to describe characteristics and treatments of patients with HER2-mutated locally advanced/metastatic NSCLC initiating first-line (1 L) therapy between January 1, 2015, and March 31, 2024, in a real-world setting. Endpoints included real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS) and overall survival (OS) by line of therapy and in subgroups of interest. RESULTS: Of 158 patients included (median age 69 years, 43.0% with Y772_A775dup [YVMA] mutation), 50.6% had ≥ 2 lines of therapy. Common 1 L therapies were chemotherapy + immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI; 36.1%) and chemotherapy (27.8%); common second-line (2 L) therapies were ICI (23.8%), chemotherapy + ICI (16.3%), and HER2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC; 16.3%). Median rwPFS/OS was 5.7/17.5, and 4.3/11.2 months, following initiation of 1 L and 2 L treatment, respectively. Median rwPFS ranged from 4.4 to 8.9 months and median OS from 15.7 to 16.0 months, following initiation of 1 L chemotherapy with or without ICI. Median rwPFS following initiation of 2 L treatment with ICI ± chemotherapy, chemotherapy ± monoclonal antibody, or HER2-targeted ADC ranged from 3.0 to 4.7 months, and OS from 10.8 to 23.4 months. Outcomes appeared to be descriptively inferior in patients with YVMA mutations versus other subgroups. CONCLUSIONS: Overall outcomes were unsatisfactory, including in patients who had received chemotherapy ± ICI or HER2-targeted ADC in any line, highlighting the need for more effective targeted therapies.

papers.authors: Small C, Kumar D, Abbas A, Sánchez Fructuoso A, Yamanaga S, Pérez González VL, Karakizlis H, Nissen M et al.

papers.results: 主要终点（移植受者第2剂后1个月 vs 第1剂后1个月的中和抗体平均几何倍数升高，双剂组）：RSV-A 1.34（95%CI 1.20, 1.48；n=111）；RSV-B 1.26（95%CI 1.14, 1.40；n=111）。单剂在移植受者中具免疫原性，但初始中和应答较非免疫抑制对照更慢、总体更低，霉酚酸酯使用者尤甚。RSVPreF3特异性CD4+ T细胞频率在所有组均较基线升高。体液与细胞免疫应答在接种后12个月维持高于基线。两剂均耐受良好，安全性谱相似且可接受。摘要未报告具体不良事件率、临床疾病终点或主要终点的P值。

papers.abstract_en: Immunocompromised adults are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease. This multicountry, open-label phase 2b trial (NCT05921903) evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the AS01E-adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) over 12 months in kidney or lung transplant recipients ≥18 years, randomized 1:1 to receive one (n = 131) or two doses 30-60 days apart (n = 130). A control group of non-immunocompromised adults ≥50 years (n = 125) received a single dose. The primary outcome was the mean geometric increase in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing titers one month following a second adjuvanted RSVPreF3 dose relative to the first dose in transplant recipients. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the safety and immunogenicity of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in transplant recipients compared with the control group. In transplant recipients receiving two doses, neutralizing titers against RSV-A and RSV-B were numerically higher one month post-dose 2 than post-dose 1 (mean geometric increases: 1.34 [95% CI: 1.20, 1.48] for RSV-A [n = 111] and 1.26 [95% CI: 1.14, 1.40] for RSV-B [n = 111]). A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients, but showed slower and generally lower initial neutralizing responses than in non-immunocompromised controls, specifically in individuals receiving mycophenolate. RSVPreF3-specific CD4 + T-cell frequencies increased after vaccination versus baseline in all groups. Humoral and cell-mediated immune responses remained above baseline for 12 months post-vaccination. Both doses of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and had a similar and acceptable safety profile. Overall, these results support a favorable benefit-risk profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in kidney and lung transplant recipients.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Short-course antibiotic prophylaxis has been associated with a reduced risk of early-onset ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) in selected populations, particularly patients with acute brain injury. However, its role in severely injured trauma patients remains controversial. METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective cohort study, conducted in 15 French trauma centres, included severely injured adults who required mechanical ventilation initiated within 24 h of admission and continued for at least 48 h. Propensity score-based analyses assessed the association between early antibiotic prophylaxis (initiated within the first 24 h of management and continued for up to 72 h) and patient outcomes. The primary outcome was early-onset VAP; secondary outcomes included late-onset VAP, extrapulmonary infections, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU and hospital length of stay, and 30-day mortality. RESULTS: A total of 1,321 trauma patients were included. Antibiotic prophylaxis was administered to 746 patients (56%), with amoxicillin-clavulanic acid used in more than 90% of cases. Early-onset VAP occurred in 240 of 746 patients (32%) who received antibiotic prophylaxis and in 195 of 575 (34%) who did not. After inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), antibiotic prophylaxis was not associated with early-onset VAP (weighted odds ratio [wOR] 0.87, 95% CI 0.66-1.22; p = 0.48). A cause-specific Cox model accounting for the competing risk of death before day 7 yielded similar results (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR] 0.87, 95% CI 0.71-1.07; p = 0.19). Antibiotic prophylaxis was not associated with improve of secondary outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Routine antibiotic prophylaxis in severely injured trauma patients was not associated with a reduced risk of early-onset VAP. CLINICALTRIALS: Gov ID NCT07059039 - Registration date: July, 10th 2025.

papers.abstract_en: This study combines RNA sequencing data from 1,824 tumors across major lung cancer types to examine how tumor gene expression patterns relate to histologic diagnoses. The resulting reference landscape identifies nine transcriptional clusters, including a neuroendocrine-like adenocarcinoma group and regions with mixed histology. The clusters also show associations with clinical features, genetic alterations, immune characteristics, and survival. An interactive Oncoscape resource allows researchers to explore the integrated data and compare patient tumors with patient-derived xenograft models.

papers.title_zh: 右心导管检查中踏车运动与单臂动态运动的血流动力学比较：臂部运动方案强度不足，血流动力学反应显著小于踏车，不能替代
papers.title_en: Hemodynamic effects of cycle ergometry versus dynamic unilateral arm exercise during right heart catheterization: a prospective observational study.
papers.authors: Berezucki E, Heinrich M, Rueß A, Lange TJ, Perl M, Stadler S
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Internal Medicine II, University Medical Center Regensburg, Franz-Josef-Strauß-Allee 11, 93053, Regensburg…
papers.results: mPAP升高：CE 12 mmHg vs AE 3 mmHg（p<0.001）；PAWP升高：CE 5 mmHg vs AE 2 mmHg（p<0.001）；心输出量升高：CE 2.2 L/min vs AE 0.6 L/min（p<0.001）；mPVR变化：CE 下降 0.05 WU（p=0.761），AE 下降 0.32（p=0.03）；AE期间估计VO₂仅达CE增量的24%，相当于约6 W外部负荷；运动中无患者PAWP升至>25 mmHg；静息无肺高压者中CE诊断出5例运动性肺高压（EPH），而所用AE方案不适合检出EPH
papers.authors_conclusion: AE proved to be a safe exercise modality in our study but, with the protocol applied here, produced significantly smaller hemodynamic changes during RHC than CE and is thus not an adequate substitute in this form, leaving open whether an intensity-matched protocol could achieve comparable hemodynamic effects.
papers.ai_note: 核心方法学疑点：两种运动方式强度不匹配（AE由患者自定强度，VO₂仅达CE的24%，约等效6 W），因此组间血流动力学差异很可能主要反映运动强度差异而非运动方式本身，无法据此否定强度匹配后的AE；作者亦自认强度匹配方案未验证。AE组mPVR显著下降而CE组不显著，方向上进一步提示AE强度不足而非保护性效应。无患者PAWP>25 mmHg，可能同样源于运动强度不足。EPH检出仅报'5例'，缺分母、检出率及CI，EPH诊断效能无法评估；EPH阈值（mPAP/CO斜率>3 mmHg·L⁻¹·min⁻¹）未报CE与AE各自的阳性例数对比。样本量小（n=50），摘要无CI

pico.p: 连续入组的50例有右心导管检查（RHC）指征的患者
pico.ic: 踏车运动（CE，固定做功10–50 W）对比动态单臂运动（AE，强度由患者自定）；同一患者内休息后随机顺序运动，热稀释法测心输出量

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The reintroduction of exercise pulmonary hypertension (EPH) to the pulmonary hypertension (PH) definition by the European guidelines underlines the importance of examining the hemodynamic response to exercise during right heart catheterization. Because the standard exercise modality of cycle ergometry (CE) is not universally accessible, we compared its hemodynamic effects with those of dynamic single-arm exercise (AE) in patients undergoing right heart catheterization (RHC). METHODS: 50 consecutive patients with indication for RHC were enrolled. Hemodynamic parameters were assessed at rest, followed by randomized exercise periods with an intervening rest phase. Thermodilution was used to determine cardiac output. The intensity of the AE was patient-determined, whereas CE was conducted at a fixed work rate ranging from 10 to 50 watts, based on the patient's physical status. Oxygen uptake (VO₂) was estimated using the reverse Fick principle to compare relative exercise intensity between modalities. EPH was defined by an mPAP/cardiac output slope > 3 mmHg·L⁻¹·min⁻¹, and exercise-induced left heart disease by a rise in PAWP from ≤ 15 mmHg at rest to > 25 mmHg during exercise. RESULTS: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure increased by 12 mmHg with CE compared to 3 mmHg with AE (p<0.001), pulmonary artery wedge pressure increased by 5 mmHg versus 2 mmHg (p<0.001), cardiac output increased by 2.2 L/min versus 0.6 L/min (p<0.001) and mean pulmonary vascular resistance decreased by 0.05 WU with CE (p=0.761) and by 0.32 with AE (p=0.03). Estimated VO₂ during AE reached only 24% of the increase observed during CE, corresponding to an external workload equivalent of approximately 6 W. No patient showed an increase in pulmonary artery wedge pressure during exercise above 25mmHg to unmask left heart disease. In patients without PH at rest, CE led to the diagnosis of EPH in 5 patients while the used AE protocol was not suitable to detect EPH. CONCLUSION: AE proved to be a safe exercise modality in our study but, with the protocol applied here, produced significantly smaller hemodynamic changes during RHC than CE and is thus not an adequate substitute in this form, leaving open whether an intensity-matched protocol could achieve comparable hemodynamic effects.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Bronchiectasis is a chronic inflammatory airway disease with limited disease-modifying therapies. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects, but their impact on bronchiectasis outcomes remains unknown. RESEARCH QUESTION: Is GLP-1RA use, compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor (DPP-4i) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) use, associated with better clinical outcomes in patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes (T2D)? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Using the TriNetX global federated research network, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes who initiated GLP-1RA therapy between June 1, 2022, and May 30, 2025. We compared clinical outcomes, including all-cause mortality, bronchiectasis exacerbation, acute respiratory failure, and lower respiratory tract infections, with patients receiving DPP-4i) or SGLT2i using propensity score matching to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 1,029 patients per group were included in the GLP-1RA versus DPP-4i cohort, and 2,255 patients per group in the GLP-1RA versus SGLT2i cohort. Compared with DPP-4i, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.43; 95% CI, 0.33-0.56) and reduced risks of acute respiratory failure (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.36-0.58) and lower respiratory tract infection (HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.46-0.65). Similar benefits were observed compared with SGLT2i for all-cause mortality (HR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.40-0.60), acute respiratory failure (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.39-0.55), and lower respiratory tract infection (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.68-0.86). Stratified analyses demonstrated consistent mortality benefits across demographic and clinical subgroups, with particularly pronounced effects in obese patients but there was no statistically significant reduction in bronchiectasis exacerbations. INTERPRETATION: Among patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA therapy was associated with significantly lower mortality and reduced respiratory complications compared with DPP-4i or SGLT2i. These findings suggest potential disease-modifying benefits of GLP-1RAs in bronchiectasis beyond glycemic control.

papers.title_en: The Burden of Chronic Cough in Patients With Interstitial Lung Disease: a US Survey-Based Analysis of Its Effects on Daily Life and Emotional and Social Well-Being.
papers.authors: Swigris J, Kulkarni T, Watterston C, Nakano A, Barrett K, Shore JE
papers.affiliation_highlight: National Jewish Health, Denver, CO, USA.
papers.results: 197名参与者完成调查；75.63%自报IPF，21.32%非IPF ILD，3.05%待确诊。过去一周内76.15%报告咳嗽干扰日常活动，79.69%报告睡眠中断。95.94%有咳嗽引起的担忧，75.13%有抑郁、悲伤或情绪低落，67.01%因咳嗽回避社交场合；60.91%报告慢性咳嗽影响柏拉图式关系，55.33%报告影响维持身体或亲密关系的能力或意愿。治疗方面历史上平均使用2.7个治疗类别，目前使用2.0个类别，许多人报告缓解有限或无缓解。
papers.authors_conclusion: Findings from this US survey of patients with IPF or non-IPF ILD and chronic cough indicate that, among respondents, chronic cough burden manifests physically, psychologically, and psychosocially. Reports of limited relief from available therapies suggest an unmet need in managing chronic cough in this patient population.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic cough (≥8 weeks) is highly prevalent among patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and non-IPF interstitial lung disease (ILD) and imposes significant physical, social, and psychological burden. Research characterizing the burden of chronic cough in patients with IPF and non-IPF ILD from the patient perspective is limited. RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the multidimensional burden of chronic cough in patients living with IPF or non-IPF ILD? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: An online cross-sectional survey was distributed to adults from June to July 2025 via the Pulmonary Fibrosis Foundation's US Community Registry. Eligibility required a self-reported diagnosis of IPF or non-IPF ILD and chronic cough. Multiple-choice and open-text questions spanned six domains: demographics, disease history, cough characteristics, daily life impact, social/emotional and long-term impact, and healthcare experience. RESULTS: A total of 197 participants completed the survey: 75.63% reported a diagnosis of IPF, 21.32% reported non-IPF ILD, and 3.05% were awaiting further ILD diagnosis. Participants reported cough-related interference with daily activities (76.15%) and sleep disruption (79.69%) within the preceding week. Emotional burden was frequently reported: 95.94% of participants had cough-induced worry, 75.13% had depression, sadness, or low mood, and 67.01% reported avoiding social situations because of cough. Additionally, 60.91% of participants reported that chronic cough affected their platonic relationships, and 55.33% reported impact on their ability or desire to maintain physical or intimate relationships. To treat cough, participants reported using an average of 2.7 therapeutic classes historically and 2.0 classes currently, with many reporting limited or no relief. INTERPRETATION: Findings from this US survey of patients with IPF or non-IPF ILD and chronic cough indicate that, among respondents, chronic cough burden manifests physically, psychologically, and psychosocially. Reports of limited relief from available therapies suggest an unmet need in managing chronic cough in this patient population. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: The 6-minute walk test (6MWT) is widely used to assess functional capacity in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, individual test components remain underutilized despite their independent prognostic value. We aimed to evaluate a 6MWT-derived index for predicting long-term mortality and exacerbation risk in COPD. METHODS: We analyzed 2063 COPD patients from the prospective Korean COPD Subgroup Study. The STEP (Speed Terminate Early Performance) index combined gait speed (<1.0m/s), early test termination, and the distance-saturation product (<290m%). The primary outcome was 10-year all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included respiratory and cardiovascular mortality, exacerbations, and symptom trajectories. Discrimination was compared with the BODE and BODEx indices using Harrell C-index and time-dependent AUCs. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses are a major cause of morbidity in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet little is known about their incidence, risk factors, and transmission dynamics in community settings. We aimed to compare the epidemiology of multiple respiratory viruses within households in the Gambia. METHODS: We conducted a prospective household cohort study in a peri-urban region of the Gambia. Households with ≥5 members, including at least one adult and one child, were enrolled and followed for one year. Upper respiratory tract swabs were collected weekly, regardless of symptoms, and tested by RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2, seasonal coronaviruses, human rhinovirus (HRV), influenza A/B, RSV A/B, parainfluenza viruses 1-4, human metapneumovirus, and adenovirus. We estimated incidence, symptomatic fraction, shedding duration, and household secondary attack rates (SARs), and explored associations with virus type and demographic variables. FINDINGS: From 2 March 2021 to 13 June 2022, 349 participants from 52 households completed 14,421 scheduled and 129 unscheduled visits. Respiratory viruses were detected in 11.1% of visits (n = 1611), representing 1423 infection episodes. HRV was most common, infecting 86.5% of participants (2.4 infections per person-year). Children aged <5 and 5-17 years shed virus for longer than adults (p = 0.0005), with longer shedding durations seen for HRV and SARS-CoV-2. Overall, 88.4% of infections were asymptomatic, with the highest symptomatic proportions for SARS-CoV-2 (16.3%) and RSV (17.7%) (p = 0.03). We found evidence for reductions in incidence risk with increasing age for HRV, RSV, seasonal coronaviruses, and parainfluenza viruses, with no difference for SARS-CoV-2. Among 719 index infections, the mean household SARs for all viruses combined was 6.7%. Infection with prolonged shedding (p = 0.002), specific viral species (p < 0.0001) and a lower Ct value were associated with increased transmission. INTERPRETATION: A large burden of asymptomatic infections underlies the circulation of respiratory viruses within households, with key differences in incidence, shedding and transmission across viral species. FUNDING: This study was funded through a UK Research and Innovation grant.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: There is no standard second-line treatment for patients with platinum-refractory advanced B3-Thymoma (T) and thymic carcinoma (TC). In this population, the PECATI trial (NCT04710628) testing the combination lenvatinib and pembrolizumab met its primary endpoint, with 5-month progression-free survival (PFS) of 88.0%. Here we report the final clinical study results. METHODS: PECATI is a single-arm, phase 2 trial enrolling patients with metastatic B3-T and TC, without autoimmune disorders that have progressed following at least one platinum-based chemotherapy. The trial evaluated lenvatinib (20 mg orally once daily) plus pembrolizumab (200 mg iv infusion once every 3 weeks) in 3-week cycles for a maximum of 35 cycles if no disease progression or toxicity. RESULTS: 43 patients were enrolled: median age 57 years (33-81); 84% had a TC; 65% Masaoka Koga IVB, 51.2% of patients with ≥3 metastatic sites, and 44.2% received ≥2 prior lines for advanced disease. After a median follow-up of 24.6 months, the median PFS was 22.1 months (95%CI: 10.9-25.1), and the median overall survival (OS) was 40.2 months (95%CI: 19.1-not estimated), with 36-month OS rate of 53.0%. Two (4.7%) non-treatment-related grade 5 events were reported. The rate of grade 3 immune-related adverse events was 11.6%. CONCLUSION: The final results of PECATI trial supports the combination lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab as a potential treatment option in pre-treated advanced B3-thymoma and thymic carcinoma. Toxicity profile is manageable but close monitoring is advised.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) remains one of the most common and serious complications among mechanically ventilated patients in the ICU. Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are considered a vulnerable population for VAP because of impaired immune function and metabolic dysregulation. This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models for the early prediction of VAP in mechanically ventilated ICU patients with T2DM. METHODS: A total of 876 mechanically ventilated ICU patients with T2DM from the MIMIC-IV database were included and randomly divided into training and testing sets at a ratio of 7:3. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression, and Spearman correlation analysis. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) was applied to address class imbalance. Four ML models, including logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), gradient boosting machine (GBM), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), were developed. Model performance was comprehensively evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and multiple performance metrics, including recall, specificity, and F1-score. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were applied to interpret the optimal model, and a web-based risk calculator was further developed. In addition, sensitivity analyses were performed by retaining the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score and using the original dataset without SMOTE to evaluate the robustness of the model. RESULTS: A total of 876 patients were included, of whom 73 developed VAP and 803 did not. XGBoost demonstrated the best predictive performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.891 (95% CI 0.862-0.920), a recall of 0.832, a specificity of 0.877, and an F1-score of 0.851 in the testing set. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and DCA indicated favorable potential clinical net benefit. SHAP analysis identified the seven most influential predictive features in the model, including Glucose_max, SOFA-Renal score, hypertension, Temp_min, Scr_max, WBC_min, and SOFA-CNS score. CONCLUSION: Four ML models were developed and compared for the early prediction of VAP in mechanically ventilated ICU patients with T2DM, among which XGBoost demonstrated the best predictive performance. SHAP improved the interpretability of the model and identified the seven predictive features that contributed most to model predictions. Future prospective multicenter external validation studies are needed to further evaluate the model's generalizability and provide additional evidence for the early risk assessment of VAP in patients with T2DM.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Despite improved survival with targeted therapies and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), evidence regarding the risk and economic burden of drug-induced interstitial lung disease (DI-ILD)-a potentially fatal adverse event-remains limited. We evaluated drug- and generation-specific risks of DI-ILD and its associated economic burden. METHODS: Using the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service (HIRA) claims database (January 1, 2012-May 31, 2023), we identified patients treated with ICIs, epidermal growth factor receptor inhibitors (EGFRis), or anaplastic lymphoma kinase inhibitors (ALKis). Incidence rates (IRs) and hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for ILD were estimated using stabilized generalized propensity scores weighting and Cox proportional hazards models. After 1:4 propensity score matching, healthcare costs and resource utilization during ILD treatment period were compared between patients with and without ILD. RESULTS: Among 12,744 ICI users, 44,689 EGFR and 5,655 ALK prescription records, 111, 178, and 33 cases of ILD were identified, respectively. Compared with nivolumab, pembrolizumab (HR, 2.14; 95% CI, 1.12-4.11) and atezolizumab (HR, 1.80; 95% CI, 0.96-3.38) showed higher ILD risk. First- (HR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.44-1.00) and third-generation EGFRis (HR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.22-0.89) had significantly lower risks than second-generation EGFRis. Compared with third-generation ALKis, first-generation (HR, 0.15; 95% CI, 0.03-0.70) and second-generation ALKis (HR, 0.20; 95% CI, 0.04-0.89) showed significantly lower risks of ILD. ILD was associated with higher healthcare costs and utilization, including hospitalization costs (2.11-5.24 times), infection and respiratory medication costs (2.72-13.88 times), hospitalization admissions (1.69-3.84 times), length of stay (1.66-2.57 times), and emergency room visits (1.21-5.58 times). CONCLUSION: Given the substantial economic burden DI-ILD imposes, understanding differential risks of DI-ILD across treatment options could inform treatment selection and enable more timely management.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint blockade has reshaped lung cancer treatment, yet durable benefit remains restricted to a subset of patients. Biomarkers incompletely capture interactions between immune activation and tumor-intrinsic resistance. Integrating immune and epithelial expression programs may help identify response-associated states and candidates for functional investigation. METHODS: Public bulk transcriptomes were analyzed with format-specific preprocessing, empirical Bayes differential expression, standardized cross-cohort evidence, and gene-set enrichment. Five discovery-informed modules formed an immune-resistance score. Conditional leave-one-out and leave-cohort-out analyses refitted normalization within training data and compared the fixed score with a nested ridge-logistic model. Survival, composition-adjustment, and prioritization sensitivity analyses were performed. Single-cell counts underwent quality control, unsupervised clustering, and patient-level pseudobulk analysis. MAL2 was investigated in A549 and H1299 cells using knockdown, growth, motility, apoptosis, HLA-ABC, cytokine, and PBMC co-culture assays. RESULTS: No individual gene met FDR <0.05 in any of the three discovery contrasts. Favorable-response genes were enriched for adaptive immune processes, whereas the unfavorable list showed weaker DNA-replication enrichment. Conditional leave-cohort-out AUCs for the dual-axis score were 0.964, 0.859, and 0.773; performance did not consistently exceed the immune axis. In GSE190266, outcome analysis yielded a cohort-relative AUC of 0.617 with incomplete module coverage. Higher scores were associated with longer PFS in two evaluated cohorts. Quality control retained 91,762 single cells. MAL2 remained epithelial-enriched and ranked third among 58 evaluable candidates, but its patient-level epithelial response contrast and standalone PFS associations were not significant. Knockdown reduced growth and motility-related readouts, increased apoptosis and HLA-ABC expression, and altered cytokine and co-culture activation readouts. CONCLUSION: The immune-resistance framework links cohort-level response patterns to epithelial candidates for functional investigation. MAL2 depletion alters growth and immune-related phenotypes in lung cancer cells, supporting further investigation of its biological role.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) pathogenesis is heterogeneous with important contributions from impaired upper airway anatomy and at least three key non-anatomical endotypes. Detailed physiology assessments in a relatively small number of well-characterized participants indicate wide interindividual variability in pharyngeal collapsibility and that ~70% have impairment in one or more non-anatomical endotype. In this study, we applied recently developed models that use standard clinical and polysomnography data to estimate OSA endotypes and oral appliance therapy response in a large clinical population. METHODS: OSA endotypes and oral appliance therapy responses were estimated using standard sleep study outputs and clinical data (age and BMI) from > 6500 consecutive home-based diagnostic studies with an Apnoea/Hypopnea Index (AHI) > 5 events/h (Sleep Profiler PSG-Advanced Brain Monitoring). The proportion of participants who were estimated to have impairment in one or more OSA endotypes was calculated according to previously published physiological cutoffs. RESULTS: On average, participants (39% female) had moderately severe OSA (AHI = 28 ± 23 events/h [Mean ± SD]), were middle aged (49 ± 16 years) and obese (BMI = 31 ± 7 kg/m2). 29% were estimated to have only mild anatomical compromise. 23% had poor dilator muscles, 31% high loop gain and 29% had a low arousal threshold. 62% had severe ("bad") impairment in one or more non-anatomical endotypes. ~60% were predicted to respond to oral appliance therapy. CONCLUSIONS: These novel data highlight the heterogeneity of OSA in a large clinical OSA patient population and the feasibility for endotype-informed precision medicine for OSA via application of novel physiology-based algorithms using home sleep study recordings at scale.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: While lung transplantation (LTx) is an established therapy for end-stage lung disease in an aging population, lung cancer (LC) complicates the transplant journey. This study aimed to elucidate factors associated with LC development and post-diagnosis mortality. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center observational study at a certified lung cancer center of patients with primary LC after LTx between 1997 and 2025. Characteristics, survival and predictors of development of LC and mortality were assessed. RESULTS: Of 2,541 LTx recipients, 47 developed LC, corresponding to an incidence of 1.9%. The median time from LTx to LC diagnosis was 6.05 [3.44-8.89] years. Age at transplantation was 55 [IQR 45-59] years; donor age was 52 [46-60] years. Most tumors arose in the transplanted lung (N = 33, 70%). Survival following LC diagnosis was 0.57 [0.22-1.64] years. Unilateral LTx (HR 2.89), donor smoking history (HR 1.82), ILD/pulmonary fibrosis (HR 1.49), older recipient age (HR 1.37 per 10 years), and cumulative recipient smoking exposure (HR 1.13 per 10 pack-years) were associated with LC development. Stage-IV disease (HR 2.56), unilateral LTx (HR 2.13), prolonged time to LC diagnosis (HR 2.09), and advanced donor age (HR 2.03) were associated with mortality. CONCLUSION: Lung cancer after LTx is a rare complication with poor prognosis. Recipient-, donor, and transplant-related characteristics were associated with LC development, while advanced-stage disease and selected transplant-related factors were associated with mortality. Screening protocols should be intensified in an aging LTx population.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Longitudinal evidence on the association of dietary patterns with lung function and COPD risk is limited and inconclusive. We examined whether adherence to a dietary pattern aligned with the latest Nordic Nutrition Recommendations (NNR2023) was associated with lung function, longitudinal change in lung function and risk of developing COPD. METHODS: In total 5,520 individuals, 58% women, mean ± SD age 50±13 years, with baseline dietary data and spirometry measurements (2006-08 and 2017-19) were included from the Trøndelag Health Study. We constructed a dietary adherence index from nine NNR2023-relevant food and beverage categories. COPD was defined as pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1)/forced vital capacity (FVC) <the lower limit of normal in individuals aged ≥40 years. Clinical COPD additionally required respiratory symptoms and ≥10 pack-years. Associations were examined using multivariable regression analyses adjusted for lifestyle- and demographic covariates. RESULTS: Adherence to the NNR-aligned dietary pattern was associated with better lung function at baseline and lower odds of incident clinical COPD, OR: 0.86 (95% CI: 0.78-0.96). Each 1-point increase in the index corresponded to 11 mL higher FEV1 and 14 mL higher FVC. Among ever-smokers, the OR was 0.90 (95% CI: 0.80-1.00) after additionally adjustment for smoking status and pack-years. Baseline diet did not predict longitudinal changes in lung function, or incident spirometry-defined COPD. CONCLUSION: A healthy dietary pattern was positively associated with baseline lung function but not with longitudinal change in lung function or incident spirometry-defined COPD. Results for incident clinical COPD remains uncertain.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Inhaler technique errors are common and associated with poorer disease control. Clinicians assess technique against device-specific checklists that differ in content, limiting comparisons across inhaler types. OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate the Portsmouth Inhaler Technique (PIT) Score, a standardised, device-neutral assessment tool for adults and children. METHODS: Inhaler technique steps were extracted from 418 published and NHS checklists and underwent three rounds of Delphi essentiality assessment by 18 experts, followed by relevance (34 experts) and clarity (62 assessors, including inhaler users) evaluation. Discriminant validity was examined by comparing PIT Scores, derived retrospectively for 677 adults in an observational study, with Asthma Control Questionnaire (ACQ6) or COPD Assessment Test (CAT) scores. Twenty-two experts assessed 14 standardised videos representing seven different inhaler devices to evaluate reliability; 20 repeated the assessment. RESULTS: Seventy-two steps were refined over three rounds into a 16-step checklist with ten scored and six unscored steps. All steps met the relevance threshold (I-CVI ≥0.78); average scale-level content validity was 0.95. PIT Scores showed no meaningful correlation with ACQ6 (ρ=0.008; p=0.858) or CAT (ρ=0.077; p=0.267), supporting discriminant validity. Inter-rater reliability was excellent (Gwet's AC1=0.9177; ICC=0.9015), as was intra-rater agreement (AC1>0.92). Median PIT Score completion time was 58 seconds. CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, the PIT Score is the first reliable clinician-observed assessment tool applying one set of scored steps to all inhaler types. Its ten scored steps give a practical, standardised record of technique across devices. Prospective evaluation in routine practice, in children and against clinical outcomes is needed.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a chronic respiratory disorder characterized by recurrent upper airway collapse, associated with increased cardiometabolic risk and symptoms of depression and anxiety, whereas insomnia is characterized by persistent sleep difficulties and emotional and cognitive impairments. OBJECTIVE: To analyze the available scientific evidence on the effects of different physical training protocols on mental health outcomes, particularly symptoms of depression and anxiety, in individuals with OSA and/or insomnia. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Randomized controlled trials that investigated physical training interventions in adults with OSA and/or insomnia and assessed mental health outcomes were included. Searches were performed in PubMed, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, Scopus, and LILACS databases. RESULTS: Of the 535 studies initially identified, five randomized controlled trials met the eligibility criteria, totaling 187 participants, predominantly sedentary adults and older adults. Three studies investigated individuals with OSA and two involved populations with insomnia. Intervention protocols were mainly based on structured aerobic exercise, particularly walking, performed at least three times per week at moderate to vigorous intensity. The studies reported significant reductions in symptoms of depression, anxiety, and fatigue, as well as improvements in sleep quality and daytime sleepiness. CONCLUSION: Regular aerobic exercise yields clinically relevant improvements in mental health and sleep outcomes in individuals with OSA and insomnia; however, the evidence remains limited by the low number of randomized trials, heterogeneous protocols, and small sample sizes.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) remains a major complication of mechanical ventilation, while the role of family members in preventive care has been insufficiently explored. This study aimed to investigate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding VAP among family members of intensive care unit (ICU) patients. METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted among family members of ICU patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation at the Yueyang Hospital of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine from July 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. Demographic characteristics and knowledge, attitude, and practice scores were collected and assessed using a self-designed structured questionnaire. The cutoff for good knowledge, positive attitudes, and proactive practices was defined as at least 70.0% of the corresponding total score. Descriptive analysis, multivariable regression, and structural equation modeling (SEM) were performed to evaluate factors associated with KAP outcomes and explore relationships among KAP domains. RESULTS: A total of 406 participants were included, with 56.9% being female. The mean knowledge, attitude, and practice scores were 3.48 ± 5.26 (possible range: 0-24), 38.94 ± 6.62 (possible range: 10-50), and 19.33 ± 6.50 (possible range: 7-35), respectively. SEM showed direct effects of knowledge on attitude (β = 0.190, p < 0.001) and practice (β = 0.222, p < 0.001), as well as a direct effect of attitude on practice (β = 0.329, p < 0.001). Knowledge also indirectly affected practice through attitude (β = 0.063, p = 0.001). CONCLUSION: Family members of ICU patients generally held poor VAP-related knowledge, positive attitudes, and poor practices. Knowledge and attitudes were key determinants of preventive practices, with attitude mediating the knowledge-practice pathway. Structured family-oriented education and bedside participation protocols should be integrated into ICU care to improve feasible VAP-prevention behaviors.

papers.abstract_en: Acute lung injury (ALI) is characterized by excessive inflammatory responses and macrophage dysfunction, yet effective pharmacological therapies remain limited. In this study, we identified magnolol (MGN), that possesses potent anti-inflammatory activityas a primary prototype component of SHHS with potent anti-inflammatory activity. However, its role in ALI remains unclear. The results showed that MGN administration at three doses (20, 40, and 80 mg/kg), significantly attenuated pulmonary edema and histopathological damage, accompanied by a reduction in macrophage-mediated inflammation in a model of LPS-induced ALI, with reductions in TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 levels varying across endpoints. The 80 mg/kg dose showed the most consistent protection. Moreover, MGN reduced iron-dependent lipid peroxidation in lung macrophages, suggesting that it may attenuate ferroptosis-associated changes. Furthermore, transcriptomic analysis combined with functional assays demonstrated that MGN suppresses ferroptosis-associated changes and subsequent macrophage inflammation, potentially through increased expression of carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1 A (CPT1A). Targeted LC-MS/MS analysis further revealed changes in intracellular carnitine and C16/C18 acylcarnitines, supporting an effect on CPT1A-associated carnitine metabolism. Mechanistically, pharmacological inhibition and siRNA-mediated knockdown of CPT1A markedly diminished the ability of MGN to suppress lipid peroxidation and pro-inflammatory cytokine production in vitro, indicating that CPT1A-associated regulation may contribute to the protective effects of MGN. Collectively, these findings suggest that MGN warrants further investigation as a potential treatment for ALI and indicate that CPT1A-associated metabolic regulation and ferroptosis-related responses might contribute to the protective effects of MGN in macrophages.

papers.abstract_en: Widespread detection of 6:2 chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonic acid (6:2 Cl-PFESA), a major substitute for perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS), has been reported in various environmental and human biological samples. Yet, its lung inflammation and sex-dependent effects have not been studied. In this study, mice were orally gavaged a single dose of 10 mg/kg/BW 6:2 Cl-PFESA or vehicle control for 28 days. Males exhibited greater susceptibility than females, as evidenced by earlier body weight loss, more severe lung histopathology, elevated inflammatory cytokine expression, and increased pulmonary lipopolysaccharide accumulation. The transcriptomic analysis also showed extensive sexual dimorphism, with a significantly larger number of differentially expressed genes in the female lungs compared with males, with minimal overlap between sexes. The NOD-like receptor signaling pathway was identified as a major responsive pathway, with upregulation of NLRP12 in both sexes and sex-specific down-regulation of Interferon regulatory factor 7 (Irf7) in males and Bcl-2-like protein 1 (Bcl2l1 (Bcl-xL) in females. In vitro siRNA-mediated knockdown of NLRP12 in A549 and THP-1 cells confirmed its role as a positive mediator of the 6:2 Cl-PFESA-induced inflammatory response. Furthermore, 6:2 Cl-PFESA promoted NLRP12 inflammasome-associated activation, characterized by enhanced NLRP12 expression, caspase-1 cleavage, mature IL-1β processing, increased IL-18 secretion, and elevated caspase-1 enzymatic activity. Notably, 6:2 Cl-PFESA significantly altered the lung microbial community, enriched by Proteobacteria and depleted by Firmicutes and Bacteroidetes. Pro-inflammatory genera, including Stenotrophomonas (e.g., S. maltophilia) and Chryseobacterium (e.g., C. indologenes), were enriched predominantly in males. Collectively, these findings identified NLRP12 inflammasome-associated signaling and sex-dependent microbial dysbiosis as key mechanisms underlying male-biased lung inflammation, informing sex-specific risk assessment of PFAS alternatives.
